title: Drivers, Passengers & Pedestrians
citation: NJTR-1 Crash Report Manual (2023), Appendix: General Questions
key_points: Someone seated in a vehicle is an occupant even if their feet are on the ground; someone half in or half out while standing up or sitting down is a pedestrian.
Riders in a cargo area are position 10; people riding on or hanging onto the outside are position 11 (box 84).
Pedestrians and cyclists don't get driver's license numbers in boxes 32/62.

faq.q: When does someone getting out of a parked car become a pedestrian?
faq.a: If they're seated, they're an occupant, even with their feet on the ground. If they're in the middle of standing up or sitting down, half in and half out, they're a pedestrian. If they're standing on the vehicle with their feet off the ground, they're a passenger.

faq.q: How do I list someone riding in a pickup bed, or who falls off the back of a trash truck?
faq.a: In the cargo area: code 10. Riding on or hanging onto the outside: code 11.

faq.q: Someone jumps onto the outside of a car and the driver takes off.
faq.a: List it as a motor vehicle crash with a passenger riding on the outside: code 11.

faq.q: A 16-year-old with a permit is driving with a parent. Whose information goes where?
faq.a: The permit driver's information goes in the driver boxes (26-34 or 56-64). Put the supervising parent's information in the crash description (box 145).

faq.q: Do I enter the license of an emergency vehicle driver, or a volunteer responding in a personal car?
Do pedestrians or cyclists get a license number entered?
Do pedestrians get Sequence of Events?
faq.a: No. Sequence of Events describes what the motor vehicles did. Record the pedestrian's actions in Pre-Crash Action.

faq.q: A car runs a cyclist off the road but never touches them. Is that a crash?
faq.a: No. Without contact with the vehicle in transport, it isn't a crash.

faq.q: A cyclist grabs onto a moving car for a tow, falls and is hurt.
faq.a: List them as a pedalcyclist. In the narrative, explain that they were holding onto the vehicle and whether the driver knew.
